items.title: `intent://` handling in `shouldOverrideUrlLoading` → arbitrary activity launch / redirection
items.vrt: `broken_access_control.exposed_sensitive_android_intent` (null, rated on what it reaches) → P1-class when it reaches a private component/file grant
items.attacker: AM-02 (web content already in the WebView)
items.applies_to: any WebView not hard-blocking non-`http(s)` schemes in `shouldOverrideUrlLoading`
items.maps_to: local corpus Class #19; `risks/unsafe-uri-loading`, `risks/intent-redirection`; gap-adversary "web content reaching Intent.parseUri"
items.test:
Boundary: this item is the WebView-client side (web content → `shouldOverrideUrlLoading` → `parseUri` →
`startActivity`); the router-side `intent://` arriving through a deep link is D09-065 and the local-app delivery is
D08-022 / D08-024 — the grep and the clear-check are recorded once, here. The handler does `Intent.parseUri(url, 0)`
+ `startActivity` without resetting component/selector, so **web
content already loaded in the app's WebView** (an allow-listed CDN, an ad frame, an OAuth page) can navigate to
`intent://` and make the app launch non-exported same-app activities — with the app's UID, no other app involved.
items.how:
```bash
  grep -rn 'shouldOverrideUrlLoading' $DEC/jadx/sources -A20 | grep -nE 'parseUri|startActivity'
```
From a page the WebView loads:
```html
<script>location = "intent://x/#Intent;component=com.target/.InternalSettingsActivity;S.debugFlag=1;end";</script>
```
The `SEL` selector to force an unexpected action is honoured by WebView and Firefox but blocked by Chrome.
items.proof:
The non-exported activity resuming (`dumpsys activity activities | grep -E 'ResumedActivity'` — matches
`mResumedActivity` on Android ≤ 9 and `topResumedActivity` on 10+) with the
WebView's page URL being the attacker origin in the same capture.
items.escalation:
Combine with D08 grant flags to convert a web visit into a file read; pure remote-web path to
non-exported components (D04/D08).
items.ruled_out_when:
the handler calls `setComponent(null); setSelector(null)` and verifies the target is
exported/permitted before `startActivity`, or hard-blocks non-`http(s)` schemes.

items.title: DNS rebinding against the app's embedded localhost HTTP/WebSocket server
items.vrt: rated on what the endpoint exposes; Critical when it accepts a command reaching code execution / file write
items.attacker: AM-02 (any browser page on the phone)
items.applies_to: apps running a loopback server (NanoHTTPD, Cordova/Ionic, a stray RN dev server, a Flutter/Unity asset server, QR-pairing)
items.maps_to: `risks/bad-dns` (Insecure DNS Setup) — closest published slug (gap-adversary corpus)
items.test:
A loopback server is not protected by SOP: a web page the victim visits in any browser on the phone can be
pointed at `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/` via a rebinding name, and everything that server exposes becomes web-reachable.
items.how:
```bash
  adb shell ss -ltnp 2>/dev/null                       # find the listener
  adb shell dumpsys package com.target | grep userId=  # attribute the socket
  grep -rnE 'NanoHTTPD|ServerSocket\(|HttpServer|Ktor|embeddedServer|WebSocketServer|:8080|:8081' $DEC/jadx/sources
```
Serve a page from your domain (DNS TTL 1s) that flips the A-record to 127.0.0.1 after first load, then `fetch('/')`.
items.proof:
The response body of the app's localhost endpoint rendered inside a browser tab whose origin is your
domain — screenshot the URL bar and body together; `adb logcat` showing the app served it completes it.
items.escalation:
→ D19 if it is a framework dev server (hot-reload = arbitrary JS); → D16 if it parses attacker bytes
natively.
items.ruled_out_when:
no loopback listener exists, or the server enforces an `Origin`/`Host` allow-list and a
per-connection token that a rebound origin cannot supply.

items.title: Custom Tabs navigation-callback cross-site login oracle (web-side finding)
items.vrt: cross-site state inference — file against the *website* scope, not the app
items.attacker: AM-03 (any installed app, no permissions, no interaction)
items.applies_to: any target website whose in-scope users have its cookie in a Chromium-based Android browser
items.maps_to: SecWeb 2022 "The Bridge... is Still Broken" §IV (first known attack on Android CustomTabs)
items.test:
A malicious app launches a target site in a Custom Tab (which shares the browser cookie jar) and reads the
sequence/timing of `CustomTabsCallback` navigation events to infer the victim's state without reading the response —
status-code (4xx empty body fires `NAVIGATION_FAILED`+`FINISHED`, 200 does not), redirect (auth'd `/login`→`/home`
fires two `NAVIGATION_STARTED`/`FINISHED`), and timing (baselined against a hidden WebView, which shares no state).
items.how:
Build a PoC app registering a `CustomTabsCallback`, load the target URL, and classify the event
sequence/timing; baseline the timing against the same URL in a hidden WebView.
items.proof:
A PoC app that reliably reports "victim is logged into example.com" purely from callback sequence/timing,
verified by logging in/out of the target in the device browser.
items.escalation:
Combine with D09 to deanonymise a victim; the paper notes it opens history-sniffing doors. Trusted
Web Activities inherit the state-sharing; since androidx.browser 1.6 / Chrome 115 they also expose a `postMessage`
channel validated by Digital Asset Links — treat an app-side `PostMessageService` / `CustomTabsSession.postMessage`
handler as a bridge and rate it by what it does with web-originated messages (D10-010 rules apply; verify the origin
check reads the validated relation, not the URL string).
items.ruled_out_when:
the target site does not distinguish authenticated vs unauthenticated by status/redirect/timing
on the probed endpoints — this is a web-side finding delivered through a mobile primitive.

items.title: Predictive back inside WebView escaping the app's history guard (targetSdk 36)
items.vrt: broken flow control; High if it leaves an inconsistent server-side state an attacker exploits
items.applies_to: targetSdk 36+ WebView flows relying on `onBackPressed()`→`webView.goBack()`
items.maps_to: `about/versions/16/behavior-changes-16`; `guide/navigation/custom-back/predictive-back-gesture` (WebView codelab)
items.test:
With predictive back default-on at targetSdk 36, a WebView-hosted flow that relied on `onBackPressed()` to
intercept and call `webView.goBack()` (or to block leaving a payment page) loses the interception.
items.how:
```bash
  grep -rn 'goBack()\|canGoBack()\|onBackPressed' $DEC/jadx/sources
```
On Android 16, drive a multi-step WebView flow and swipe back.
items.proof:
The activity finishes instead of stepping back in WebView history, or the user leaves a half-completed
transaction with server-side state already mutated.
items.escalation: → D15 state-machine abuse if the abandoned server state is exploitable.
items.ruled_out_when:
the flow migrated to the `OnBackPressedCallback`/`OnBackInvokedCallback` API and correctly steps
WebView history (or the app targets < 36), and no server-side state is left inconsistent.

items.title: Trusted-origin content renders attacker HTML → the allow-list is a non-defence → bridge credential theft
items.vrt: `sensitive_data_exposure.disclosure_of_secrets.for_publicly_accessible_asset` (P1); `cross_site_scripting_xss.stored.non_admin_to_anyone` (P2) as the delivery leg
items.attacker: AM-05 (another user writes the field) / AM-02
items.applies_to: apps with a bridge attached to a first-party web origin that renders server-supplied HTML
items.maps_to: HackTricks webview-attacks.md ("Trusted-origin HTML/CRM content → bridge credential theft"); `risks/cross-app-scripting`; MASWE-0033
items.test:
A strict scheme+host allow-list (D10-016) is worthless if the *trusted* origin itself renders
attacker-influenceable HTML — CRM banners, loyalty widgets, support-chat bodies, feature-flagged marketing
fragments, previews. The allow-list passes because the origin genuinely is first-party; the injection is *on* that
origin. The chain: attacker writes a profile/campaign field (often authorised by a **public** customer identifier
leaked in invite links, API responses or app resources) → a first-party page fetches the banner/template JSON → an
SDK renders it with `innerHTML` → stored XSS on the trusted, allow-listed origin → JS calls a credential-returning
bridge (D10-004) and skims the token with a wrapped callback (D10-014).
items.how: Trace every attacker-writable field into banners, campaigns, dashboards, previews and loyalty content; check whether the backend authorises the profile read/write with a public identifier. **JSON escaping is not HTML escaping** — after `JSON.parse`, `` is live markup, so a field that looks safely JSON-encoded on the wire is not. ```bash grep -RniE 'innerHTML|outerHTML|insertAdjacentHTML|dangerouslySetInnerHTML' "$DEC/apktool/assets/www" $DEC/jadx/sources grep -RniE 'banner|campaign|template|promo|loyalty|announcement' "$DEC/apktool/assets/www" $DEC/jadx/sources | grep -iE 'html|render' ``` Set the writable field to ``, open the first-party WebView screen, then swap the payload for the callback-wrap of D10-014 to lift the session token.
items.proof:
Your server receives the JWT/session token from a page whose origin is the app's own first-party host —
request carries a `; wv` UA, the package in `X-Requested-With` and the first-party `Referer`, proving it ran in the
in-app WebView, not a browser. Because the vector is stored and cross-user, one write hits every user who views the
content.
items.escalation:
→ D10-004/D10-014 → D13/D15 ATO; the writable-field-authorised-by-public-id half is itself an
IDOR/access-control finding (D07/D13). File the stored-XSS primitive and the bridge consumer separately, then link.
items.ruled_out_when:
every server-supplied fragment the first-party page renders is HTML-escaped at the sink (not
merely JSON-encoded on the wire), no bridge method returns a credential (D10-003 negative), and attacker-writable
fields cannot reach any WebView-rendered surface.

items.title: Intent-sourced value interpolated into an inline HTML template rendered under a fixed trusted https `baseUrl`
items.vrt: `sensitive_data_exposure.disclosure_of_secrets.for_publicly_accessible_asset` (P1) when the origin carries cookies or a bridge; `cross_site_scripting_xss.reflected.non_self` (P3) floor
items.attacker: AM-02 (deep link / BROWSABLE route) / AM-03 (explicit intent with extras)
items.applies_to: apps that build HTML in Java/Kotlin string templates and call `loadDataWithBaseURL("https://<first-party>", html, …)`
items.maps_to: MASWE-0035, MASTG-KNOW-0018; `risks/cross-app-scripting`; D04-016 (the exported-activity delivery half), D09-059 (the deep-link delivery half)
items.skip_when: `grep -rlE 'loadDataWithBaseURL\("https?://' $DEC/jadx/sources | wc -l` is 0 **and** no `loadDataWithBaseURL` call has a non-null, non-literal base — notes: `D10-073 n/a: no trusted-base loadDataWithBaseURL sink`.
items.test:
The URL allow-list is irrelevant here: nothing is loaded by URL. A value that arrives via an Intent extra,
a deep-link parameter or a provider row is concatenated into the HTML/script of an inline template (embedded
player, receipt, article, promo) and rendered under a real first-party https base, so injected markup runs with
that origin's cookies, localStorage and any bridge attached to the WebView. D10-022 is an attacker-influenced base,
D10-023 a null base, D10-025 JS-string concatenation — this is the fixed trusted base, which the validator never sees.
items.how:
```bash
  grep -rn 'loadDataWithBaseURL(' $DEC/jadx/sources -B30 | grep -nE 'getStringExtra|getQueryParameter|getArguments|getData\(\)|append\(|\+ *"' | tee "$E/logs/D10-073.txt"
```
Trace each interpolated variable to its source (the D04 / D09 inventories). Confirm the base is a first-party https
URL and whether the value is attribute-escaped. Deliver with the shared probe (`start` step: explicit component plus
typed extras, D09-076) and an 8+ character marker; grep the baseline render for the marker first (D09-078).
items.proof:
The marker rendered unescaped inside the template, then a benign beacon from the page whose request carries
the first-party `Referer`, the `; wv` UA and the package in `X-Requested-With`; if a bridge is attached, its method
list from D10-003.
items.escalation:
→ D10-004 / D10-014 (bridge in the first-party origin); → D10-022 (cookies of the base origin);
→ D13 / D15.
items.ruled_out_when:
Every interpolated value is HTML/attribute-escaped (or JSON-quoted into a script context) before
concatenation, or the base is `null`/`about:blank` with no bridge and no cookies — verified by reading the template
builder, not the call site.

items.title: Native pushes a secret into page JS on page lifecycle without an origin check
items.vrt: `sensitive_data_exposure.disclosure_of_secrets.for_publicly_accessible_asset` (P1)
items.applies_to: WebViews that call `evaluateJavascript` / `loadUrl("javascript:…")` from `WebViewClient` callbacks, or `WebViewCompat.addDocumentStartJavaScript`
items.maps_to: MASWE-0033, MASTG-BEST-0035; `risks/insecure-webview-native-bridges`
items.skip_when: `grep -rlE 'evaluateJavascript\(|addDocumentStartJavaScript\(' $DEC/jadx/sources | grep -viE '/(android|androidx)/' | wc -l` is 0 — notes: `D10-074 n/a: no native→JS injection calls`.
items.test:
The value flows native → page, the opposite direction to every bridge item. If the injection fires on every
navigation (`onPageStarted` / `onPageFinished`), or the start-script origin rules contain `*`, the origin that
receives the token or config object is whatever the WebView currently shows — an off-allow-list page, a redirect
target or a cross-origin iframe gets it for free, with no bridge call at all. D10-025 is quote-breaking injection
into the string; D10-010 is the listener direction.
items.proof:
Hook output showing the token/config string injected while `getUrl()` is a non-first-party origin (or `*`
in the origin rules), plus the string's use as a credential (the D10-003 interceptor pairing).
items.escalation: → D13 / D15 replay; → D10-006 if the injection is per-frame.
items.ruled_out_when:
The injection is gated on an exact-origin check of the loaded URL at call time (or the origin
rules are an exact first-party list) **and** the injected object holds no credential — verified by the hook across
one on-list and one off-list navigation.

items.title: Covert bridge over `onJsPrompt` / `onJsAlert` / `onJsConfirm` / `onConsoleMessage`
items.vrt: inherits D10-004 (rated by what the handler returns or does)
items.applies_to: WebViews with a custom `WebChromeClient`
items.maps_to: MASTG-TEST-0334, MASWE-0033; the Cordova prompt bridge (D10-058) is the documented shape
items.skip_when: `grep -rlE 'onJsPrompt|onJsAlert|onJsConfirm|onConsoleMessage' $DEC/jadx/sources | grep -viE '/(android|androidx)/' | wc -l` is 0 — notes: `D10-075 n/a: default WebChromeClient dialogs`.
items.test:
A `WebChromeClient` override that parses the prompt/alert/console text (JSON, a `scheme:` prefix) and
dispatches to native code is a bridge with the same reach as `@JavascriptInterface` — but with no annotation, no
object name and no frame/origin information beyond the `url` argument (the main-frame URL: the D10-009 caveat
applies). It is invisible to every `addJavascriptInterface` / `addWebMessageListener` grep, so an app built this way
passes D10-003 as "no bridge".
items.how:
```bash
  grep -rn 'onJsPrompt\|onJsAlert\|onJsConfirm\|onConsoleMessage' $DEC/jadx/sources -A25 | grep -nE 'JSONObject|parse|split|startsWith|confirm\(|switch' | tee "$E/logs/D10-075.txt"
```
Build the same capability table as D10-003 (handler name → what it reads, does, returns). Runtime: hook the override,
log `url` and `message` per call while exercising the app; from a page, `prompt('<command>')` and read the return.
items.proof:
The handler inventory with return values traced; one call from a non-first-party page (via D10-016..021)
returning app data through `JsPromptResult.confirm`.
items.escalation: → D10-004 / D10-014; the `url` argument guard is D10-009.
items.ruled_out_when:
The override only shows dialogs (no parsing of the message), or every dispatch path checks an exact
origin derived from the calling frame and returns nothing sensitive — verified by reading the handler bodies.

items.title: Flutter WebView bridges: `JavaScriptChannel` and `flutter_inappwebview` handlers
items.vrt: inherits D10-004 / D10-012 by handler capability
items.applies_to: Flutter apps bundling `webview_flutter` / `webview_flutter_android` or `flutter_inappwebview`
items.maps_to: MASWE-0033, MASTG-TEST-0334; the plugin sources (`webview_flutter_android` registers each `JavaScriptChannel` through `addJavascriptInterface` under the channel name; `flutter_inappwebview` exposes `JavaScriptBridgeInterface` with `javaScriptBridgeOriginAllowList` / `javaScriptHandlersOriginAllowList` options)
items.skip_when: `ls $DEC/apktool/lib/*/libflutter.so 2>/dev/null | wc -l` is 0 **or** `grep -rlE 'webview_flutter|flutter_inappwebview|JavaScriptChannel|JavaScriptBridgeInterface' $DEC/jadx/sources $DEC/apktool/assets/flutter_assets 2>/dev/null | wc -l` is 0 — notes: `D10-076 n/a: not Flutter / no Flutter WebView plugin`.
items.test:
Channel and handler names are declared in Dart (the AOT snapshot); the Java side is generic plugin code the
package-exclusion greps skip. The bridge object is injected into every frame with no origin check unless the app set
the plugin's origin allow-list option. Rate by what the Dart consumer does with the message (token, file, payment,
navigation) — the framework fast-paths D10-055..062 cover Capacitor, Cordova and React Native; this is the Flutter one.
items.how:
```bash
  strings "$DEC/apktool/lib/arm64-v8a/libapp.so" | grep -iE 'channel|handler|postMessage|callHandler' | sort -u | tee "$E/logs/D10-076.txt"   # channel / handler names from the Dart snapshot
  strings "$DEC/apktool/lib/arm64-v8a/libapp.so" | grep -iE 'javaScriptBridgeOriginAllowList|javaScriptHandlersOriginAllowList|allowFileAccessFromFileURLs|allowUniversalAccessFromFileURLs|useShouldInterceptRequest'   # the plugin options the app set
```
Runtime: the D10-003 `addJavascriptInterface` hook lists the channel objects and names; then enumerate
`window.<channel>` / `window.flutter_inappwebview` from a page reached via D10-016..021 and post a message.
items.proof:
The channel/handler inventory with the Dart-side consumer named; a message posted from a non-first-party
page producing an observable native effect or a returned value.
items.escalation:
→ D10-004 / D10-014; file-access options re-enabled → D10-031 / D10-032; the Dart/Java two-parser
differential → D09-047.
items.ruled_out_when:
Every channel's Dart consumer ignores or validates the message origin (the plugin origin
allow-list set to exact first-party origins) and no handler returns a credential or performs a privileged action —
verified from the snapshot strings and the runtime enumeration.

items.title: First-party session cookies reachable from a third-party SDK WebView (no profile isolation)
items.vrt: `sensitive_data_exposure.disclosure_of_secrets.for_publicly_accessible_asset` (P1) when the SDK WebView can be steered to attacker content; otherwise chain fuel
items.applies_to: apps with two or more WebView owners (first-party plus an ad / support / analytics SDK)
items.maps_to: MASTG-KNOW-0018; androidx.webkit `Profile` / `ProfileStore` (multi-profile WebView)
items.record: logs/D10-077.txt (cookie scope: which WebView sent which cookie to which host)
items.skip_when: `inventory/webviews.csv` lists only first-party owners, **or** `grep -rlE 'ProfileStore|setProfile\(' $DEC/jadx/sources | wc -l` is ≥ 1 and every SDK WebView is assigned a non-default profile — notes: `D10-077 n/a: single owner / profiles isolated`.
items.test:
Without the androidx.webkit multi-profile API (`ProfileStore` / `WebViewCompat.setProfile`) every WebView in
the process shares one cookie and storage store, so an SDK WebView that loads third-party creatives sends the
first-party session cookie with every request it makes to a first-party host. Log in (cookie-based web session), then
drive the SDK WebView (ad creative, help centre, chat) to a request to the first-party host or to an open redirect on
it; combine with any D10-066 / D10-067 script-execution vector to read the rows where `is_httponly=0` (D10-046).
items.how:
```bash
  grep -rn 'CookieManager.getInstance()' $DEC/jadx/sources | grep -vE '/jadx/sources/(android|androidx)/'
  grep -rlE 'ProfileStore|setProfile\(|setDataDirectorySuffix' $DEC/jadx/sources
```
Proxy the SDK WebView's traffic and inspect the `Cookie:` header on first-party hosts.
items.proof:
The SDK WebView's request to a first-party host carrying the session cookie in the proxy, plus the absence of
any profile assignment in code.
items.ruled_out_when:
SDK WebViews run in a separate profile (or a separate process with `setDataDirectorySuffix`), or
the first-party session is not cookie-based for any host the SDK WebView can reach.
